hook: Why do our muscles feel sore days after working out?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.5] Petter, why do my legs hurt two days after lifting?
HOST: [expr:0.7] That is delayed onset muscle soreness, or DOMS! When you exercise, you create microscopic tears in your muscle fibers. It sounds intense, but it is actually awesome!
GUEST: [expr:0.6] Micro-tears sound pretty painful though!

HOST: [expr:0.8] Think of your body like a construction crew! Day one is clearing out old structures. Day two is when the crew brings in trucks of protein to rebuild stronger walls. The inflammation during rebuilding causes that deep ache. So when you waddle down stairs, just remember your body is upgrading itself!

hook: How do noise-canceling headphones actually block sound?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.5] Hey Petter, how do these headphones cancel noise?
HOST: [expr:0.7] Oh, it is total physics magic! Tiny microphones on the outside listen to ambient sounds, like a roaring plane engine, and instantly analyze the sound wave.
GUEST: [expr:0.6] So they just play loud music over it?

HOST: [expr:0.8] Not at all! The headphones create an exact opposite sound wave, flipped completely upside down. When a peak wave hits a valley wave, they clash and cancel each other out to absolute zero sound! It is literally math fighting noise in real time!

hook: Why does a brain freeze happen when eating cold food?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.5] Petter, what causes an instant brain freeze?
HOST: [expr:0.7] It is your body throwing a total false alarm! When icy slush hits the roof of your mouth, the sudden temperature drop startles sensitive blood vessels.
GUEST: [expr:0.6] Do the blood vessels freeze up?

HOST: [expr:0.8] They slam shut, then rapidly dilate to pump warm blood back in! That rapid swelling triggers a major nerve behind your palate. But here is the funny part: that nerve gets confused and tells your brain that your forehead hurts instead! Pressing your warm tongue to your palate resets the system!
